senses.gloss: gleanings; the poor man’s share in the crop (Lev. XIX, 9).
units: Ib. 10 איזהו ל׳ הנושר וכ׳ what is called leḳet (the poor man’s share)? That which drops &c.
Ib. 11 ספק ל׳ ל׳ where there is a doubt about leḳet, it is leḳet, i.e. the poor man has the benefit of the doubt.

<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 5:1">Ib. V, 1</cite> <he>אומדין אותה כמה ל׳ וכ׳</he> we calculate how much it would ordinarily give out for the poor man. Y. ib. V, beg. 18ᵈ <he>שגדש ע״ג לִיקְטָן של וכ׳</he> for he piled up the stack over the poor man’s share; a. fr.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 26b:2">M. Kat. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>הקורע … מתוך הל׳</he> he who rends his garment … in a place which has been mended by a pucker (after having been rent for a death).
